new_symbol_range_suggestions.kappa_inf: positive; e.g. 1/10 to 100, with smaller values giving stronger heterogeneity-induced curvature and the parent recovered as kappa_inf -> oo

derivation_notes: Relax the assumption that all infectious units have identical infectivity by treating episode-level infection opportunity as a Poisson process with a gamma-distributed effective hazard across infectious units or micro-opportunities. Marginalizing that heterogeneity gives a negative-binomial/Lomax-type survival law, preserving monotone saturation but changing log-survival curvature with cumulative exposure.
change_summary: The equal-infectivity exponential law is replaced by a heterogeneous-effectiveness survival law with shape parameter kappa_inf. This changes the scored mapping itself: p_inf remains increasing in q, D, and tau, but low- and high-exposure regimes no longer share one constant log-survival slope.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: All infectious units have the same average ability to initiate infection.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Biological heterogeneity in infectious-unit viability or access to susceptible target sites makes effective infection-initiation propensities distributed rather than identical.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: As kappa_inf -> oo, (1 + beta_inf*q*D*tau/kappa_inf)**(-kappa_inf) -> exp(-beta_inf*q*D*tau), recovering the parent law.

response_change.parent_relation: The parent maps cumulative exposure only through the linear product q*D*tau inside one exponential, so log-survival is proportional to dose and duration with a single shared slope.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the assumption of equal per-unit infectivity with heterogeneous infectious-unit effectiveness, so increasing D or tau changes risk with a different convexity/concavity pattern in the survival curve while preserving monotone saturation.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed q, the rise of p_inf with cumulative exposure q*D*tau is no longer governed by one constant hazard slope: low-exposure and high-exposure regimes differ systematically in curvature, which a single refitted beta_inf cannot match across both regimes.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when experiments span at least about an order-of-magnitude range in cumulative effective exposure q*D*tau, so departures from a single linear log-survival slope are resolvable while environmental conditions remain fixed.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate variation in D and tau can already reveal nonconstant curvature against cum_exp; in holdout, more extreme low or high cumulative exposures amplify the same heterogeneous-infectivity effect rather than introducing a new mechanism.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: If infectious units become effectively homogeneous, the heterogeneity parameter tends to its parent limit and the child law reduces to p_inf = 1 - exp(-beta_inf*q*D*tau).
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Biological heterogeneity in infectious-unit viability or access to susceptible target sites causes the effective per-unit infection-initiation propensity to be distributed rather than identical, changing how infection probability accumulates with dose and duration.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the added shape parameter changes the functional form of survival from a single exponential to a finite-capacity-like saturating power law in cumulative exposure, producing exposure-dependent curvature rather than a uniform gain rescaling.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: All infectious units have the same average ability to initiate infection.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Infectious units have heterogeneous effective infection-initiation propensities, represented by a finite-shape mixed-hazard law.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: As kappa_inf -> oo, the child expression converges to 1 - exp(-beta_inf*q*D*tau).
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Holding environment fixed and varying D and tau so that q*D*tau spans low to high values, the parent predicts linear negative log-survival with one shared slope beta_inf, whereas the child predicts curvature: early increments in cumulative exposure and later increments contribute differently to p_inf, while risk still increases monotonically toward 1.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set can only produce log(1 - p_inf) = -beta_inf*q*D*tau, which is exactly linear in cumulative exposure for all admissible conditions. The child produces log(1 - p_inf) = -kappa_inf*log(1 + beta_inf*q*D*tau/kappa_inf), whose slope with respect to q*D*tau decreases with exposure. Therefore refitting beta_inf alone cannot simultaneously match both low-exposure and high-exposure curvature across one shared dataset when D and tau vary over a broad range.

evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Biological heterogeneity in infectious-unit viability or access to susceptible target sites causes the effective per-unit infection-initiation propensity to be distributed rather than identical, changing how infection probability accumulates with dose and duration.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the equal-infectivity assumption already present in the parent rather than adding a new process. The parent response is a simple exponential dose-time law: holding environment fixed, p_inf increases monotonically with D, tau, and q, and the entire mapping is controlled by the single product q*D*tau with one shared slope beta_inf. The child would keep the same inputs and monotonicity but allow heterogeneous infectious-unit effectiveness, which changes the target mapping itself by altering curvature of p_inf versus cumulative exposure, not merely an auxiliary latent quantity. Concrete distinguishing condition: vary D and tau over a broad admissible range while holding environmental conditions fixed and comparing low versus high cumulative exposures at the same q. Under the parent, a single refitted beta_inf forces one linear relation in negative log-survival versus q*D*tau, so it cannot simultaneously fit systematically different low-exposure and high-exposure curvature. This contrast is scientifically admissible when cumulative exposure spans enough range for heterogeneity to matter; if experiments remain confined to a narrow low-risk regime, the refinement may be weakly identifiable and the parent may approximate it well.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.gamma_adapt: positive; e.g. 1/1000 to 10 in inverse(infectious-unit*hour), with gamma_adapt*D*tau spanning much less than 1 in weak-modulation episodes and order 1 or larger when adaptation is active

derivation_notes: Assume instantaneous susceptibility during the episode decays with accumulated burden: q_eff(s) = q*exp(-gamma_adapt*D*s) under constant dose D. Integrating the infection-initiation hazard over s from 0 to tau gives an effective burden proportional to q*D*Integral(exp(-gamma_adapt*D*s), s=0..tau) = q*(1 - exp(-gamma_adapt*D*tau))/gamma_adapt, which replaces the parent's q*D*tau term inside the same heterogeneity-saturating map.
change_summary: The fixed-within-episode susceptibility assumption is relaxed so susceptibility wanes during exposure as burden accumulates. This breaks the parent's exact collapse onto q*D*tau and creates a dose-duration interaction: at matched D*tau, higher D activates depletion earlier and lowers risk.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Host susceptibility remains fixed during an exposure episode.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Acute exposure-triggered depletion or temporary refractoriness of immediately infectable target cells reduces effective susceptibility as exposure accumulates within the episode.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: As gamma_adapt -> 0, (1 - exp(-gamma_adapt*D*tau))/(gamma_adapt*D) -> tau, recovering the parent law exactly.

response_change.parent_relation: The parent depends on dose and duration only through the cumulative product q*D*tau, so any (D,tau) pairs with the same product give the same infection probability after refitting one shared parameter set.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the assumption that host susceptibility stays fixed during the episode by allowing susceptibility to wane with ongoing exposure burden, so infection probability depends on dose and duration separately rather than only through q*D*tau.
response_change.observable_effect: At equal cumulative exposure D*tau, short-high-dose episodes produce lower risk than long-low-dose episodes because susceptibility is reduced earlier under intense exposure, flattening the dose response at large D more than the duration response at proportionally matched tau.

evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: The new law couples dose intensity and duration inside an exponential attenuation before the outer saturation, so no single rescaling of beta_inf or kappa_inf can preserve matched-product predictions while also fitting intensity-dependent departures from collapse.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Host susceptibility remains fixed during an exposure episode.

evolution_contract.parent_reduction: As gamma_adapt -> 0, the factor (1 - exp(-gamma_adapt*D*tau))/(gamma_adapt*D) tends to tau, recovering the parent expression.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.gamma_spread: positive; e.g. 1/100 to 10, with gamma_spread -> 0 recovering the single-timescale parent and order-1 values giving visibly smeared adaptation onset when gamma_adapt*D*tau is order 1

derivation_notes: The parent hazard uses a single exponential adaptation factor, equivalent to all infectable opportunities sharing one depletion rate. Here that rate is distributed with a gamma-family shape controlled by gamma_spread, whose Laplace transform gives an effective adaptation factor ((1 + gamma_spread*gamma_adapt*D*tau)**(1/gamma_spread) - 1)/(gamma_adapt*D*tau), producing a broader onset of refractoriness while preserving monotone risk growth.
change_summary: I relaxed the assumption of one common within-episode adaptation timescale by promoting the spread of adaptation onset to a measurable host-condition input gamma_spread. This changes the curvature of p_inf across D and tau, especially when gamma_adapt*D*tau is order 1, without changing the target or model family.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Host susceptibility depletion within an episode is governed by one shared rate gamma_adapt for all infectable opportunities.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Inter-individual or within-host heterogeneity in short-timescale target-cell refractoriness causes adaptation to turn on over a range of burdens rather than at one common exponential timescale.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: As gamma_spread -> 0, (1 + gamma_spread*gamma_adapt*D*tau)**(1/gamma_spread) -> exp(gamma_adapt*D*tau), so the successor reduces to the parent expression.

response_change.parent_relation: With fixed q, the parent maps cumulative burden through a single adaptation timescale gamma_adapt, so for each D the p_inf-versus-tau rise has one smooth bend and a single intensity-controlled saturation pattern.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the single waning-timescale assumption by a distributed susceptibility-loss onset across the exposure, so the effective hazard transitions from an early less-adapted phase to a later more-adapted phase more gradually; this changes the curvature of p_inf as a joint function of D and tau while preserving monotonicity.
response_change.observable_effect: At matched cumulative exposure D*tau, low-D long-tau episodes and high-D short-tau episodes separate more strongly in an intermediate regime because adaptation onset is smeared rather than locked to one exponential timescale; the parent with one shared parameter set cannot match both the early-time rise and the later-time flattening across those conditions.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Visible when gamma_adapt*D*tau is order 1, so adaptation is neither negligible nor fully saturated; weak-modulation episodes with gamma_adapt*D*tau << 1 collapse back toward the parent behavior.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, varying D and tau already probes the same total burden at different intensities; in holdout, the contrast extends to more extreme D-versus-tau tradeoffs where a smeared adaptation onset alters curvature beyond what one-timescale adaptation can fit.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the susceptibility-loss onset distribution collapses to a single timescale, equivalently zero spread around gamma_adapt.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: A distributed adaptation onset requires one independently varied host-condition descriptor controlling how broadly susceptibility-loss times are spread across immediately infectable targets; existing D, tau, and q set exposure burden and mean susceptibility but cannot identify whether curvature changes come from mean adaptation rate or heterogeneity in adaptation timing.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Inter-individual or within-host heterogeneity in short-timescale target-cell refractoriness causes adaptation to turn on over a range of burdens rather than at one common exponential timescale.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: The added input gamma_spread enters by combining with gamma_adapt*D*tau inside a power-law transform before feeding the existing saturation map, so the target mapping gains a genuine shape parameter for intermediate-burden curvature rather than a simple gain rescaling. This nested nonlinearity changes how D and tau trade off at fixed burden, which a coefficient-only correction to beta_inf, kappa_inf, or gamma_adapt cannot reproduce over one shared fit.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The current model assumes all immediately infectable target opportunities in a host lose susceptibility with the same single exponential timescale during the episode.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Adaptation onset is distributed across infectable opportunities, with spread controlled by gamma_spread, so susceptibility loss turns on over a range of burdens rather than one common timescale.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: As gamma_spread -> 0, the inner factor ((1 + gamma_spread*gamma_adapt*D*tau)**(1/gamma_spread) - 1) converges to exp(gamma_adapt*D*tau) - 1, recovering the parent law exactly.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: With D and tau independently varied while environment and fixed parameters are held constant, the child predicts a different intermediate-regime p_inf separation for episodes sharing similar D*tau but differing in D versus tau composition. The parent gives one single-phase curvature family controlled only by gamma_adapt*D*tau, whereas the child adds gamma_spread-dependent curvature broadening that is observable when gamma_adapt*D*tau is around unity and fades as gamma_spread -> 0 or gamma_adapt*D*tau << 1.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot absorb this change because refitting beta_inf only rescales hazard, refitting kappa_inf only changes outer saturation shape, and refitting gamma_adapt shifts one common adaptation timescale. None creates an independent spread parameter for the onset of adaptation, so the parent cannot simultaneously match the child's earlier less-adapted rise and later more-gradual flattening across multiple D-versus-tau tradeoffs at matched burden.

scenario_text: Estimate the probability that a susceptible person becomes infected during a single exposure episode. The independently varied conditions are inhaled pathogen dose, exposure duration, and host susceptibility, while environmental conditions remain fixed. Infection risk rises with cumulative exposure but approaches an upper bound because probability cannot exceed certainty. The benchmark targets the episode-level risk rather than subsequent disease progression.
promotion_reason: A distributed adaptation onset requires one independently varied host-condition descriptor controlling how broadly susceptibility-loss times are spread across immediately infectable targets; existing D, tau, and q set exposure burden and mean susceptibility but cannot identify whether curvature changes come from mean adaptation rate or heterogeneity in adaptation timing.

response_change.parent_relation: With fixed q, the parent maps cumulative burden through a single adaptation timescale gamma_adapt, so for each D the p_inf-versus-tau rise has one smooth bend and a single intensity-controlled saturation pattern.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the single waning-timescale assumption by a distributed susceptibility-loss onset across the exposure, so the effective hazard transitions from an early less-adapted phase to a later more-adapted phase more gradually; this changes the curvature of p_inf as a joint function of D and tau while preserving monotonicity.
response_change.observable_effect: At matched cumulative exposure D*tau, low-D long-tau episodes and high-D short-tau episodes separate more strongly in an intermediate regime because adaptation onset is smeared rather than locked to one exponential timescale; the parent with one shared parameter set cannot match both the early-time rise and the later-time flattening across those conditions.

derivation_notes: The parent kernel is re-derived by assuming that accumulated burden is less effective at generating further infectable opportunities when instantaneous dose intensity is high, representing compounded depletion or refractoriness of remaining targets. This yields an effective burden argument gamma_adapt*D*tau/(1 + gamma_crowd*gamma_adapt*D), which preserves the low-burden limit and reduces to the parent as gamma_crowd -> 0.
change_summary: Changed the within-episode adaptation law so attenuation depends jointly on cumulative burden and exposure intensity rather than burden alone. This creates stronger concavity in tau for high-D episodes while leaving the low-burden regime close to the parent.

assumption_audit.mechanism: As exposure burden accumulates, remaining infectable opportunities become progressively harder to realize at higher instantaneous dose intensity because depletion or refractoriness compounds, strengthening attenuation of later exposure contributions.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent in the limit gamma_crowd -> 0, and approximately in the weak-adaptation regime gamma_adapt*D*tau << 1 with gamma_adapt*D also small.

response_change.parent_relation: With fixed environment, p_inf depends on D and tau through a single monotone cumulative-burden adaptation law: increasing D or tau always moves risk along one shared smooth saturation shape set by gamma_adapt, gamma_spread, beta_inf, and kappa_inf.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the current adaptation kernel's implicit assumption of indefinitely increasing cumulative effective contact opportunity with a stronger burden-dependent attenuation of incremental infection opportunity, so that high-D short exposures and low-D long exposures with similar D*tau no longer lie on the same curvature family.
response_change.observable_effect: At low burden the child matches the parent, but once gamma_adapt*D*tau is order 1 or larger, risk rises less with further tau at high D than the parent predicts, producing stronger concavity in tau and a dose-dependent distortion of iso-risk curves.

evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate variation in D and tau already reveals monotone but intensity-dependent bending; in holdout, the same mechanism extends to more extreme high-D or long-tau regimes where attenuation of added exposure becomes stronger without changing the low-burden limit.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the weak-adaptation limit gamma_adapt*D*tau << 1, or by taking the added nonlinear attenuation back to the parent's current kernel form.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model treats acute susceptibility depletion with one specific smeared-onset form, effectively imposing a single-phase adaptation geometry for all exposure intensities once burden is summarized through the existing kernel.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Within-episode susceptibility depletion follows the current generalized-exponential burden kernel with a fixed shape across all dose-duration combinations.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: As exposure burden accumulates, remaining infectable opportunities can become progressively harder to realize than implied by the current kernel because refractory or depleted target availability compounds, strengthening attenuation of later exposure contributions.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the exact mathematical form of the already-present within-episode adaptation process rather than adding a new biological pathway. The parent already includes monotone adaptation, but it forces a single response family: once D, tau, q vary under fixed environment, all risk curves are governed by one shared burden-to-opportunity transform. The scientific gap is that target depletion/refractoriness may intensify as susceptible opportunities are consumed, causing later increments of exposure to contribute less than the current kernel allows. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not only an auxiliary latent trajectory: for the same fixed q and environment, varying D and tau can reveal that high-dose short episodes flatten with tau more sharply than lower-dose longer episodes of similar D*tau. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot generally reproduce both the low-burden near-parent behavior and the stronger high-burden curvature if the discrepancy is specifically an intensity-dependent reshaping rather than a global gain or timescale shift. The effect is admissible and observable when gamma_adapt*D*tau is around 1 or larger; for very small burden the distinction is weak, which is also the natural continuation path back to the parent.

derivation_notes: The parent treats within-episode susceptibility depletion as following one fixed-shape accumulation kernel. Here that burden kernel is nested inside an additional exponent so that once exposure burden has started to deplete easy-to-infect opportunities, later burden contributes progressively less, yielding stronger long-duration flattening while preserving the same low-burden limit.
change_summary: A fixed single-phase adaptation law was relaxed to a sharper self-reinforcing depletion law by introducing the curvature parameter gamma_hard. This changes the observable mapping p_inf(D,tau,q) mainly at moderate-to-large gamma_adapt*D*tau and high D where crowding already amplifies attenuation.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed q, risk rises monotonically with cumulative exposure through one adaptation phase whose attenuation strength changes smoothly with D but has a single shared curvature pattern over tau.
response_change.child_relation: Keep the same monotone saturation structure but replace the current adaptation kernel with a steeper late-exposure attenuation law, so risk initially follows the parent at short tau and low burden, then bends over more sharply at longer tau when cumulative burden is high.
response_change.observable_effect: For matched short-duration data, the refined model predicts stronger flattening of p_inf versus tau at high D than at low D, with a larger long-duration dose-duration interaction than the parent can realize using one shared parameter set.
